findings.description: [AI-SAST via Code Scan Verification Validation | claude-opus-5] encode_token (:54-76) issues a fresh identifier per token using secrets.token_urlsafe(16), a CSPRNG, so identifiers are unique and unpredictable; the algorithm is a module literal (:21) and is never read from the token header; decode_token (:89-98) requires exp/sub/iat/jti/iss/aud and verifies signature, issuer and audience, so only a server-generated token is recognised. invalidate_issued_tokens (:79-86) advances token_version, the stateless equivalent of resetting the old session on a credential or privilege change | verdict=pass confidence=high

[AI-SAST via Code Scan Verification Validation | claude-opus-5] update_user_password (:59-78) calls invalidate_issued_tokens on every password change, so all previously issued credentials stop being recognised at the moment of the privilege/credential change; create_access_token (:212-215) delegates issuance to the single jwt_tokens module so a second code path cannot mint a token with different properties | verdict=pass confidence=high

[AI-SAST via Code Scan Verification Validation | claude-opus-5] logout (:15-58) records the presented token's jti in RevokedToken with its expiry so the credential stops being honoured server-side rather than remaining valid until expiry, and additionally clears the access_token/csrf_token cookies and emits Clear-Site-Data. Repeat logout is idempotent via IntegrityError rollback | verdict=pass confidence=high

findings_aggregated_for_sde.desc: [AI-SAST via Code Scan Verification Validation | claude-opus-5] Session identity is a stateless JWT minted fresh at each authentication, so there is no pre-existing session to fixate. app/jwt_tokens.py:54-76 generates a unique jti with secrets.token_urlsafe(16) (CSPRNG, not predictable), pins HS256 rather than reading the token header, and caps lifetime at MAX_EXPIRY; :89-98 requires and validates exp/sub/iat/jti/iss/aud so a server-issued token is the only one recognised. :79-86 invalidate_issued_tokens() bumps token_version, and app/apis/auth/utils/utils.py:59-78 calls it on every password change, which is the stateless equivalent of regenerating the identifier after a credential/privilege change. app/apis/auth/services/logout_service.py:15-58 revokes the presented jti server-side and clears cookies plus Clear-Site-Data | verdict=pass confidence=high
